mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-64.1 to -58.0), indicating an established recovery trend; this momentum is expected to persist, pushing mean RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the last four.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite the prior 3-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 15 percentage points above baseline, it signals households are spending markedly less time at home, freeing discretionary time for shopping and leisure trips that lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 19.7 to 17.1 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 15 but RETAIL_REC does not rise within the following two weeks, or falls instead.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility jointly indicate restored commuting patterns, which combine with incidental shopping trips during commutes to produce a larger lift in RETAIL_REC than either factor alone over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved steadily over last 3 weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise concurrently but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: During an active reopening regime, continued recovery of PARKS mobility reflects loosening public restrictions; this policy easing extends to retail venues, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks of sustained PARKS gains.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -86.6 to -82.6 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not increase relative to the prior 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July seasonal warmth typically drives increased outdoor and retail activity; the steady rise in PARKS mobility is a seasonal proxy that will co-move with RETAIL_REC, producing higher retail mobility over the next four weeks regardless of other triggers.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is mid-July, a summer seasonal period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean fails to rise despite continued PARKS increase during the summer period.

mechanism_narrative: If week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT decelerates to less than 0.5 points (compared to the prior ~1-point weekly gains), it signals commuting recovery is plateauing, which will cap further RETAIL_REC gains within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls below 0.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly gains shrank from 1.0 to 0.7 points over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT's weekly gain falls below 0.5 but RETAIL_REC still rises in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between GROCERY_PHARM stabilizing near baseline and WORKPLACES continuing to recover suggests essential-trip saturation combined with returning commuters shifts consumer spending toward discretionary retail, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly change under 1 point while WORKPLACES rises over 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM gains slowed from 1.4 to 1.3 points while WORKPLACES gained ~1.5-2.3 points weekly
failure_condition: Both conditions hold but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state summer regime with no new restriction signals, residual improvement in RESIDENTIAL (declining toward baseline) reflects normalized seasonal routines that will continue to modestly raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined steadily from 19.7 to 17.1 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues its decline but RETAIL_REC's 2-week mean does not increase relative to the prior 2 weeks.
